summary_html: An intake **screen** is elevated to a formal **investigation/assessment** under state criteria. CAPTA and CFSR establish the federal expectations for screening, timelines, and investigative quality.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — screening/investigation conditions for funding  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal performance/quality review framework

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: In re Interest of Xandria P.
key_cases.holding: The court held that the child's recorded child-advocacy-center forensic interview was properly admitted under the rule 803(3) medical diagnosis or treatment exception and that the State proved the allegations of the § 43-247(3)(a) petition by a preponderance of the evidence.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion traces the escalation from school report through forensic interview and safety and risk assessments to a filed petition.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that the State sustained the adjudication petition by a preponderance of the evidence

key_cases.case_name: In re Interest of Borius H.
key_cases.holding: The court reaffirmed that every motion for an ex parte temporary detention order must be supported by an affidavit of a person with knowledge, held that the State must prove the requirements of Neb. Rev. Stat. § 43-254 by a preponderance of the evidence at the detention hearing, and ordered dismissal because the State adduced no evidence at that hearing.
key_cases.relevance: Escalation from report to State custody cannot rest on the caseworker's say-so; the court requires a sworn factual predicate.
key_cases.quote: we once again state that all motions for ex parte temporary detention orders must be accompanied by an affidavit of one who has knowledge of relevant facts warranting temporary detention

key_cases.case_name: In re Interest of Carmelo G.
key_cases.holding: The court held that a delay of more than eight months between entry of an ex parte temporary custody order and the protective custody order was unreasonable and violated the mother's procedural due process rights.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion describes safety plans put in place when a child is at risk of removal absent services, and the escalation from safety plan to protective custody.
key_cases.quote: due process rights include the right to be free from an unreasonable delay in providing a parent a meaningful hearing after the entry of an ex parte temporary custody order

key_cases.holding: The court held that in a hearing under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 28-723 to expunge, amend, or remove a Central Registry report the Department must prove the report's accuracy and consistency by a preponderance of the evidence, that the child-care provider had no protected property interest in her license and no cognizable procedural due process or equal protection claim, and affirmed the refusal to expunge her court-substantiated report.
key_cases.relevance: The court sets out the statutory sequence the agency must follow — report received, investigation conducted, and only then a case status determination — which is the escalation from screening to a formal investigative finding.
key_cases.quote: the Department must prove the accuracy and consistency of a Registry report of child abuse or neglect by a preponderance of the evidence

search_keywords: Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services

state_agency.name: Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services, Division of Children and Family Services

mandatory_reporters: Any person (universal mandatory reporting) — Neb. Rev. Stat. § 28-711(1)
Inspector General of Nebraska Child Welfare (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 50-1805)
reporting_details: Nebraska is a universal mandatory reporting state: any person who has reasonable cause to believe a child has been subjected to child abuse or neglect must report it to law enforcement or to the department on the statewide toll-free hotline (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 28-711(1)).

other: Dependency (no child maltreatment has been identified, however the parent or caregiver is, or will be unable to care for the child through no fault of the parent or caregiver)
